data.narrative:
Anduril Industries, a Series H defense and security company founded by Palmer Luckey and others, is currently valued at $61B following $11B+ in cumulative fundraising. The valuation assessment draws on a comparables universe of 10 peers (2 public, 8 private) operating in the Defense & Security sector, with primary focus on three same-sector, similar-valuation-tier private companies: Helsing ($18.0B, Series E), Castelion ($13.0B, Series C), and Shield AI ($12.7B, Series G).

The peer-median method is the applicable triangulation approach given available data. The three-company median valuation is $13.0B, with a range spanning $12.7B to $18.0B. This method directly reflects comparable financing activity and stage-adjusted positioning within the defense tech market.

The triangulated valuation range is $11.1B (low) to $14.9B (high), with a median of $13.0B. The current $61B valuation sits substantially above peer medians and comparable ranges. Key uncertainties include the limited peer sample size (n=3) and meaningful stage dispersion within that cohort—Helsing is Series E while Castelion is Series C—which creates valuation compression risk. Additional pricing pressure derives from market-wide defense sector volatility and the sensitivity of this asset class to geopolitical and procurement environments.
